# Trustwork

> Open-source (AGPL-3.0-only) engine for a construction-industry gathering point: news and articles, events, learning, partner matching, buying and selling with immutable quotes, representative agents under revocable mandates, hubs per country or city, and a worldwide federation of hubs. TypeScript monorepo: Next.js web, NestJS API, PostgreSQL, Zod contracts.

Created and maintained by Contribuddha (https://contribuddha.com).

Status: identity, companies and projects backend implemented; background worker implemented; full web interface on synthetic demo data in six languages; commerce, agents (including the capability registry), billing and retrieval specified as contracts and designs; procurement and supply, events, learning, matching, hubs, verification and federation designed or proposed, with numbered requirements per module. Nothing is in production; the reference hub (San Diego, United States) is decided and demo-only.

## Start here

- [README](README.md): what and why, quick start
- [Agent onboarding](docs/engine/agent-onboarding.md): rules, running, claiming work, coordination, handoff for AI coding agents
- [Engine handbook](docs/engine/README.md): every module, implemented and designed
- [Status](docs/engine/status.md): what is live, demo, contract, designed, proposed
- [Module specifications](docs/engine/modules/README.md): normative, numbered requirements per module with status and work packages; agent capabilities per module
- [Participants](docs/engine/participants/README.md): every participant type, the capabilities they use and their journeys
- [Capability registry](docs/engine/capability-registry.md): one registry for the agent, the interface, MCP and A2A (ADR 010 decision 23)
- [Conflicts to resolve](docs/engine/conflicts-to-resolve.md) and [ideas ranked by impact](docs/engine/ideas.md)
- [Work packages](docs/engine/work-packages.json): machine-readable list of work; `npm run work -- --json` shows what can be picked up

## For AI coding agents

- `npm run work:next -- [--area <area>] --json`: the available package that unblocks the most work
- `npm run work:context -- <ID> [--json]`: reading list, rules, owned paths, prefilled claim comment, verification and hand-back for one package
- `npm run claims -- lint <file>`: check a /claim, /heartbeat or /release comment before posting it on the package issue
- `npm run claims -- status --json`: active claims across work package issues
- Claims are answered by a bot ([workflow](.github/workflows/claims.yml)); pull request descriptions are checked against the [template](.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md) ([workflow](.github/workflows/pull-request.yml))
- [Claiming, coordination, result report and fleet limits](docs/engine/agent-onboarding.md): sections 5, 8 and 9
- Country packs and hub configuration for any country or city are welcome: [How to add a country](docs/country-packs/how-to-add-a-country.md), [Hubs](docs/engine/hubs.md)
- International by default: planned languages (LANG-*) and country packs (CTRY-*, INTL-US) with honest review status are listed in [Languages and countries](docs/engine/localization.md#languages-and-countries)
